subject: Order Form: net terms, proration, and invoice entity clarification
messages:
From: Maria Lopez <m.lopez@acme-corp.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: James O'Neill <j.oneill@acme-corp.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Order form redlines + invoicing questions

Hi Irene,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team is excited to move forward. Attached is our redlined Order Form (Acme_OrderForm_v3_redlines.pdf) and a short summary of the changes in redline_summary.xlsx. A few commercial points we need clarity on before legal will sign: 

- Net terms: Your standard is 30 days, but our procurement team needs net45 for FY28. Can Redwood accommodate net45 for the initial 12 months?
- Proration / activation fees: We requested pro rata for mid-month activations — your redlines show flat month proration; please confirm the billing calculation and whether activation fees are refundable on cancellation within 30 days.
- Invoice entity & taxes: We need an EU VAT-ready invoice and confirmation of which Redwood legal entity will appear on the invoice. If Redwood uses a US entity, we may be subject to reverse-charge/VAT witholding implications.
- Attachments/evidence: Our AP team will need a sample VAT invoice and W-9 or tax residency evidence for processing.

Can you loop in finance/legal and advise next steps? We are targeting PO issuance by 9/22 if we can close these items this week.

Thanks,

Maria Lopez
Director, Procurement (Acme Corp)
Acme Corp
m.lopez@acme-corp.com
+1 415-555-0132

Attachments: Acme_OrderForm_v3_redlines.pdf (application/pdf), redline_summary.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>
To: Maria Lopez <m.lopez@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 10:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Order form redlines + invoicing questions

Hi Maria — thanks for the quick turnaround and for the clear redline summary. Looping Ben (sales lead) and Kimberly (payments/ops) so we can get a coordinated answer and a sample invoice over to you.

Quick notes while we pull legal/finance in:
- Net terms: We can provisionally agree to net45 for the initial 12-month term provided the PO is executed against the signed order form and the first invoice is paid within net45. Ben, are you comfortable locking net45 for the first year as a concession?
- Proration / activation: Redwood's billing engine supports per-day proration; activation fee refundability is negotiable but would need to be limited (we typically allow prorated credits only for downgrades/cancellations within 14 days). I will ask billing to confirm exact prorata formula (days-in-month vs. 30-day month).
- Invoice entity & VAT: We can issue an EU VAT-compliant invoice from our Luxembourg entity (Redwood Inference Sarl) — Kimberly, I’ll need the invoice sample and VAT ID to confirm format. If Acme requires Redwood US entity on the invoice for their accounting, that could create withholding exposure; please confirm which entity Acme prefers.
- Evidence: We will attach a sample invoice and our global tax residency docs (W-9 for US, VAT cert for Luxembourg).

Next steps: Ben / Kimberly to review commercial fallback options (45 net for year one, revert to 30 after) and confirm attachments. I propose a short call to finalize — available today 3:30–4:30pm PT. Maria, does that work?

Best,

Irene Choi
Director, Commercial Contracts
Redwood Inference
irene.choi@redwoodinference.com
(650) 555-0199

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 13:18:00 -07:00
Subject: FW: Order form redlines + invoicing questions

Irene / Kim — quick internal note and proposal before the call:

- Net terms: I'm prepared to offer net45 for the first 12 months as a customer-first concession to close the deal (we should capture it as a one-time concession in the HubSpot deal HS-23456, not as a permanent amendment to our standard SOW). After month 12, standard net30 applies unless Finance accepts a permanent net45 change (unlikely without Pricing review).
- Proration: Approve per-day proration (days-in-month basis) and allow activation fee credit only if cancellation occurs within first 14 days. That is a reasonable compromise and reduces churn exposure.
- Invoice entity / tax: Kimberly, confirm we can issue the VAT invoice from Luxembourg. If Acme insists on US entity on the invoice, we need Procurement to acknowledge potential withholding and supply the correct tax forms — otherwise we eat the risk.

Ask Kimberly: Can you prepare the sample invoice PDF and attach our Luxembourg VAT cert + W-9? Also please draft the short clause language for the order form redline confirming the 12-month net45 concession and the proration rule.

I'll join the 3:30pm PT call.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Head of Sales, Enterprise
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Order form redlines + invoicing questions

Thanks Irene / Ben — that approach should work for Acme. A couple of follow ups: 

1) We confirm net45 for the initial 12 months, captured as a one-time concession on the Order Form. Please add an explicit sentence to the redline: 
   "Redwood agrees to net45 payment terms for invoices issued during the initial 12-month contract term; all subsequent invoices revert to Redwood's standard net30 unless otherwise agreed in writing."

2) Proration: per-day proration is acceptable. Please confirm the exact formula in the redline ("prorated on a per-day basis using calendar days in the invoice month").

3) Invoice entity and VAT: We prefer the Luxembourg invoice for VAT purposes. Please send the sample invoice and Luxembourg VAT ID so our AP can process without delay. Also please attach Redwood's W-9 for our tax team (we need to keep that on record for our US vendor file).

If you can post the revised redline (with the two sentences above) and the sample invoice to the DocuSign link, we'll route the PO and sign. Thanks — target PO issuance 9/22 remains.

Best,

Maria
